newsitem.title: USA: U.S. unions to air anti-NAFTA radio advertisements.
newsitem.headline: U.S. unions to air anti-NAFTA radio advertisements.

text.p: A U.S. labor federation will start running radio advertisements this weekend that contend the North American Free Trade Agreement (NAFTA) is taking jobs away from American workers, it said Thursday.

The AFL-CIO's Industrial Union Department, which serves 35 manufacturing unions, is sponsoring the series, which will run initially in Springfield, Illinois. The ads focus on the loss of jobs to Mexican workers under NAFTA, the union group said.
The agreement, which went into effect on January 1, 1994, links Canada, Mexico and the United States in a free-trade bloc.
The advertisements urge listeners to contact members of Congress to voice opposition to new trade legislation that would allow U.S. officials to negotiate an expansion of NAFTA to include Chile.
The labor group said Rep. John Shimkus, a Republican from Springfield, sits on the House Commerce Committee, a key panel in dealing with trade matters.

A spokesman for the union group said the anti-NAFTA ads will begin running in Washington next week. The ads will continue through September, when the administration plans to submit so-called "fast-track" trade-negotiation legislation.
Fast-track authority would speed any trade agreement through the approval process in Congress by suspending the right of lawmakers to revise a pact before a vote on whether to approve it.

"We're going to take this message across the country between now and the vote on fast track," said Peter diCicco, president of the AFL-CIO Industrial Union Department. "Congress should not allow the extension of a trade pact that already is responsible for the loss of nearly 500,000 jobs."
The White House next week is expected to send to Congress a report on NAFTA that is likely depict the trade agreement as helping the economies of all three member countries.
